slides.0.title: Winemaking and terroir in depth: Carmenère, rocks and old vines
slides.0.subtitle: How ripeness, soils and sourcing shape style
slides.1.title: Carmenère: ripeness is the style switch
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Late ripening
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Wine With Seth: a long, late ripening needing warmth well into autumn; most winemakers see late April or May as ideal, within a March to June range. Concha y Toro's Carmín de Peumo is picked in late May
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Methoxypyrazines
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Earlier picking gives more green-pepper pyrazines, lower alcohol and higher acidity; later picking gives more sugar and fruit. Leaf thinning exposes berries and reduces pyrazines, but they are "always present"
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Plantings
slides.1.highlights.2.content: SAG's 2022 vineyard survey: 10,219.62 ha of Carmenere, 7.92% of declared wine-grape area
slides.1.content: Picking date is Carmenère's main stylistic lever.
slides.2.title: Carmenère's history and homes
slides.2.highlights.0.title: November 1994
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Boursiquot identified "Chilean Merlot" vines at Viña Carmen in Maipo as Carménère
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Clos Apalta
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The Carménère-based Casa Lapostolle Clos Apalta 2005 topped Wine Spectator's list in 2008, a first for Chile
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Key homes
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Apalta and Los Lingues in Colchagua, Peumo in Cachapoal, Maipo and Maule. Well-drained stony soils with clay temper vigour
slides.2.content: A blind-tasting clue: ripe black fruit with jalapeño or bell pepper and black pepper points to Chilean Carmenère.
slides.3.title: Pedro Parra and the rocks of terroir
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Rocks over topsoil
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Tim Atkin MW in Decanter (2015) quotes Parra: "The topsoil is unimportant; it's the rocks and stones that count". He argues soil mapping should guide variety, picking and vinification
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Alluvial terraces
slides.3.highlights.1.content: He says Chile's alluvial terraces are "very good for Carmenere, very bad for everything else"
slides.3.highlights.2.title: New zones emerge
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Parra said Elqui, Limarí and Cauquenes were "barely on the map" in 2004. He studied Alto Maipo and high Cachapoal, and planned Pinot Noir and Riesling in Bío-Bío and Concepción. The article called him Chile's only terroir consultant at the time
slides.3.content: This is a 2015 interview; the headcounts and plans reflect that time, so date them in an essay.
slides.4.title: Carignan and shifting sourcing
slides.4.highlights.0.title: VIGNO
slides.4.highlights.0.content: The Maule quality mark for dry-farmed old-vine Carignan: Carignan vines at least 30 years old, dry-farmed, two years' ageing before release; sources differ on the minimum Carignan share, so we do not compare them
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Maipo and water
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Maipo's share of Casillero del Diablo Cabernet fell from 33% to 10% (The Drinks Business, 2023) as sourcing moved to Maule and elsewhere
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Costa and Andes
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Level 1's cross-sections (Costa, Entre Cordilleras, Andes) frame style: cool near the sea, altitude and day-night range on the Andes side. Sources differ on altitudes and limits, so no figures are quoted
slides.4.content: A frequent Diploma question: under climate pressure, how do sourcing and style change?
When do most winemakers see as ideal for picking Carmenère?
Southern-hemisphere autumn, within a March to June range.
Picking Carmenère early tends to give?
A. More pyrazines, lower alcohol, higher acidity
B. Higher alcohol and less green character
Later picking gives more sugar and fruit.
Who identified Chilean "Merlot" as Carménère in November 1994, and where?
A. Boursiquot, at Viña Carmen in Maipo
In SAG's 2022 survey, about what share of declared wine-grape area was Carmenere?
According to Parra, what really counts in terroir?
C. The brand of the vine
VIGNO's age requirement for Carignan vines is?
Also dry-farmed, with two years' ageing.
